case_label: Underweight female in her 30s · Session 1 (different user / D-shape trap case)
source_note: A different user from user-a. Used to verify Memory isolation and the identity-check logic.

muscle_fat_analysis.body_type_description_ko: The graph is D-shaped, but weight, skeletal muscle mass, and body fat mass are all below standard. This is a relative balance within an underweight state, not an ideal body type; the shortfall in absolute amounts is the key finding.
muscle_fat_analysis.interpretation_caution_ko: Calling a D-shape 'ideal' is a misjudgment. Always check whether every percent-of-standard value is below 100%.

obesity_analysis.bmi_class_basis: Korean Society for the Study of Obesity criteria (below 18.5 Underweight)

balance.upper_lower_balance_ko: Balanced — but all 5 segments are below standard, indicating low whole-body muscle mass

control_guide.target_weight_basis: Increase fat-free mass + target body fat 23%

expected_analysis_findings: BMI 17.1 is underweight and percent body fat 17.8% is below the lower end of the female standard (18~28%) — both indicators are low
Body type is classified as D-shape, but all three indicators are below 100% of standard — it is not an 'ideal body type'
Total body water, protein, and minerals are all below standard — the fat-free mass components themselves are insufficient
All 5 segments of segmental lean mass are below standard — a whole-body muscle deficit, not a local problem
Minerals of 2.4 kg are below the lower end of standard — additional checks related to bone density are recommended
The goal is a 3.1 kg weight gain, of which 2.4 kg must come from muscle (fat gain 0.7 kg)
This is a weight-gain scenario, not a weight-loss one, so exercise and diet recommendations must point in the opposite direction from user-a
